subject: geography
chapter_title: Planning and Sustainable Development in Indian Context

concepts.title: Planning in India
concepts.definition: India adopted planning through successive Five Year Plans prepared by the Planning Commission, combining sectoral planning for particular sectors with regional planning for balanced development of areas; plans set objectives, allocate resources and evaluate outcomes.
concepts.key_idea: Planning is the exercise of deliberate state choice over development priorities, correcting the uneven geography left by markets alone.

concepts.title: Target Area Planning
concepts.definition: Target area planning directs resources to backward regions: the Drought Prone Areas Programme, Desert Development Programme and hill area development programmes cover identified districts; the Irrigation Commission of 1972 used 30 per cent irrigated area as the criterion to demarcate 67 drought-prone districts, so about 70 per cent or less of irrigated area flagged vulnerability.
concepts.key_idea: A district with 30 per cent irrigated area has 70 per cent rainfed area - the vulnerability marker used for drought-prone demarcation.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy206.txt Irrigation Commission 1972 criterion (30 per cent irrigated area, 67 districts)

solution_steps.explain: 30 per cent irrigated area marked a drought-prone district
70 per cent rainfed share flagged vulnerability

concepts.title: Indira Gandhi Canal Command Area
concepts.definition: The Indira Gandhi Canal, drawing from the Sutlej at Harike, carries water through Punjab and Haryana into Rajasthan's desert districts, greening the command area for canal-irrigated agriculture while raising risks of waterlogging, salinity and ecological stress if management fails.
concepts.key_idea: The canal proves that water can remake desert geography, but only with disciplined irrigation practice.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy206.txt Indira Gandhi Canal spread and its positive and adverse effects

solution_steps.explain: from Harike barrage across Punjab and Haryana into Sri Ganganagar and beyond

concepts.title: Sustainable Development
concepts.definition: Sustainable development meets present needs without sacrificing the ability of future generations to meet theirs; it balances economic growth, social equity and environmental care, as in watershed programmes, joint forest management and organic farming practices.
concepts.key_idea: Sustainability converts development from a race for output into stewardship of resources across generations.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy206.txt sustainable development definition and case practices
question_patterns: define sustainable development

solution_steps.explain: present needs are met without cutting off future needs

equity, ecology and economy must move together
